claims: NYSE identity/tradability is validated; operating/backlog evidence traces to Kinder Morgan issuer reporting and current valuation is independently corroborated by market-data sources.

$10.1B project backlog is heavily natural-gas weighted and substantially tied to power/LDC demand; Q1 showed strong adjusted EBITDA/free cash flow and 3.6x leverage, while current valuation is around $70.6B market cap and ~20.5x trailing earnings.

thesisQuality.basis: Large contracted backlog and essential pipeline infrastructure support durable demand/value capture.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Q1 adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow were strong with internally funded expansion capacity.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: At about $70.6B market cap and ~20.5x trailing earnings, valuation is broadly balanced rather than clearly cheap.

catalystScore.basis: Backlog conversion and power/data-center-linked gas demand provide visible multi-year catalysts.

governancePower.basis: Internal funding and leverage discipline are constructive, though current-quarter evidence is not yet in lineage.

alignment2036.basis: Natural-gas transport supports power generation, grid reliability and industrial demand during a long-duration infrastructure transition.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Pipeline/storage networks serve power, LDC and industrial demand through reusable infrastructure.

bottleneckControl.basis: Large installed pipeline/storage networks and long permitting lead times create scarce infrastructure capacity.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Fee-based/contracted infrastructure and diversified end uses reduce direct commodity exposure.

substitutionResilience.basis: Existing pipeline networks are difficult to replicate, though electrification and alternate fuels can alter long-term throughput.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Distributed infrastructure and contracted projects provide resilience, with permitting/construction still material dependencies.

pricingPower.basis: Long-term/binding contracts and constrained transport infrastructure support durable fee economics.

riskEvidence.basis: Primary risks are permitting/construction, leverage, weather normalization and long-run demand transition rather than near-term solvency.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Primary operating/backlog evidence plus independent current valuation data provide broad coverage; Q1 operating evidence is older than preferred Q2.

scoreRecord.thesis: Kinder Morgan owns hard-to-replicate energy transport infrastructure with contracted cash flows and a backlog increasingly tied to power demand.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Demand-transition, permitting and leverage can reduce returns if expansion outruns durable contracted utilization.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Project backlog conversion and the next earnings update on leverage/backlog execution.

scoreBreakdown.note: earthScore is the Methodology 1.0 weighted component score; risk and confidence remain explicit downstream inputs.

unknowns: current Q2 leverage/backlog update not present in cumulative primary lineage
